summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would restore indexation of excise on domestically produced fuels, including gaseous fuels, as part of a wider package supporting road infrastructure funding.
Excise rates would follow the Consumer Price Index from 1 August 2014, with subsequent adjustments scheduled for 1 February and 1 August each year.
Aviation fuel would remain outside indexation, while companion bills would cover imported fuel duties, fuel tax credit calculations and a dedicated road funding account.
changes: Indexed fuel excise rates would be rounded to one decimal place of a cent.
Fuel blend calculations would use the indexed rates applying when duty on the blend becomes payable.
Production duties on stabilised crude oil and condensate would remain outside indexation.
The scheduled gaseous fuel excise increase on 1 July 2015 would be indexed and rounded.
summary.affected: Fuel manufacturers and consumers of petrol and diesel would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Christopher Pyne
speeches.brief: Moved a debate management motion limiting consideration of the four fuel indexation bills to a set process, including capping the detail stage at 30 minutes, to ensure the government's fuel excise legislation passes that day.

speeches.speaker: Ewen Jones
speeches.brief: Supported the fuel indexation bill as part of the government's election commitments, contrasting the opposition's opposition to a 0.4 cent fuel excise rise with what he said would have been a 6.85 cent per litre carbon tax on diesel under Labor, and cited a $50 billion road package over the next decade.
